# Backtest results (generated by src/backtest.py, do not edit by hand)

Leave-one-campaign-out on all 100 synthetic campaigns. Numbers come from `outputs/backtest_all_campaigns.csv`. Synthetic data, so read these as a test of the method under my assumptions, not as evidence about real Meme'd campaigns.

## All 100 campaigns

| Measure | Manual ladder (as paid) | Proposed (fraud gate on) | Proposed (no fraud gate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Campaigns over budget | 17 | 1 | 1 |
| Total overspend | ₹225,650 | ₹14,600 | ₹28,100 |
| Median share of budget used | 67% | 47% | - |
| Mean share of creators reaching rung 1 | 40% | 44% | - |
| Campaigns with rung-1 reach in 30-70% band | 45% | 77% | - |
| Median payout as share of paid-media CPM | 19% | 15% | - |
| Continuation rung1>2 / 2>3 / 3>4 | 0.43 / 0.46 / 0.21 | 0.44 / 0.46 / 0.42 | - |


The manual ladders paid ₹1,339,150 to flagged posts in total. The proposed ladders are compared on clean posts, so that saving is not credited to the ladder itself.

## Model calibration on held-out campaigns

- Realised payout of the proposed ladder was at or below the simulated P90 in 91% of campaigns (target 90%).
- Realised payout of the manual ladder fell inside the simulated P10 to P90 range in 75% of campaigns (target 80%).
